reason: E1 directly states that increased local chemical order via thermal aging enhances irradiation resistance by narrowing the mobility ratio of defects to facilitate recombination, supporting the core mechanistic premises. However, the specific aging parameters (600°C/10h), the quantitative 85% strength retention, and the high-temperature irradiation condition (~1023 K) are not explicitly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Thermal aging at 600°C for 10 hours increases local chemical order in CrCoNi
Increased local chemical order narrows the mobility gap between interstitials and vacancies
Narrowing the mobility gap enhances defect recombination
Enhanced defect recombination reduces irradiation-induced defect accumulation
Reduced defect accumulation mitigates irradiation hardening and retains yield strength
